questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on your left, what should you do?

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible to help the other driver.
Move onto the shoulder to help the other driver.
Stay in the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. Moving toward the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Moving away from it may make the other driver merge back too soon. The center is the safest position.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It stops the passing driver from returning to your lane too early.
It may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too early.
It makes the passing driver complete the pass faster.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane is dangerous. It may cause the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip opposite the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. To return to your original direction, press the opposite handgrip.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Speed up.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane can be slippery when wet because of oil deposits. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Also, slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you NOT tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid unnecessary talking or movement so you can focus on riding. They should board after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold on firmly.

questions.question: Which idea should NOT be used when planning a long group ride?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach the destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Use a staggered riding formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach the destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan routes based on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to reduce tiredness. Place inexperienced riders behind leaders so experienced riders can watch them. Use a staggered formation.

questions.question: What is a rectangular road sign?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are usually white with black lettering. They show road rules like speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What should a rider do when entering a turn?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Lean your shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down. Release the throttle and use the brakes if needed.

questions.question: When do you NOT need extra following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery.
When you cannot see past the vehicle ahead.
When weather and traffic are perfect.
When traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: When weather and traffic are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in poor conditions. Use extra space if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: How much braking power does the front brake provide?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent

questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is the right footwear for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Shoes with long, loose laces.
Shoes with short heels.
Shoes with tall heels.
Always sneakers.

questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: When a group of riders enters a highway, how should they enter?

options.text: One at a time in a single line.
In a staggered pattern.
In pairs.
Stop and wait until traffic is completely clear so all riders can enter together.

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time in a single line.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered pattern. However, when turning, going around curves, entering a highway, or exiting a highway, shift into a single-file line.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When approaching a police officer.
When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if another driver is following too closely. They may not see the hazard ahead that is making you slow down. Also flash your brake light if you are slowing down unexpectedly in a place where drivers do not expect it.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the right side of your lane so they can see you in their mirror.
On the left side of your lane to see better and be more visible.
In the center of your lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave side to side in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of your lane to see better and be more visible.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane to see better and make yourself more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: What can you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Keep your headlight on.
Reduce the space between you and other vehicles.
Weave back and forth in your lane.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and position your motorcycle where oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Maintain space around your motorcycle to move quickly if needed. Do not assume another driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.
